title: Given an array containing only 0s and 1s, rearrange it in place so that all the 0s come first followed by all the 1s, without using any extra array. (GeeksforGeeks: Segregate 0s and 1s)
shortTitle: Rearrange 0s and 1s (In-Place Partition with Two Pointers)
keyPoints: Keep a low pointer marking where the next 0 should land; sweep the array with a scanner pointer
Whenever the scanner finds a 0, swap it to the low boundary and advance the boundary
Single linear pass with O(1) extra space and no extra array
Swapping when scanner equals low is a harmless self-swap, so no special case is needed
This is the foundation of the Dutch National Flag three-way partition
Grouping is not stable: relative order within each group is not preserved

s1_definition.oneliner: Keep a boundary for the next 0, sweep once, and swap every 0 you find up to that boundary.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Rearrange 0s and 1s** – partition a binary array in place so all 0s precede all 1s.
- **Two-pointer method** – a low pointer marks the position where the next 0 should be placed; a scanning pointer sweeps left to right.
- **Swap rule** – when the scanner finds a 0, swap it with the element at low and advance low.
- **Complexity** – O(n) time, O(1) space, single pass with no extra array.
- **Foundation** – this two-value partition generalizes to the Dutch National Flag three-way partition.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of a tray of settlement slips at the National Bank of India where each slip is marked either failed (0) or cleared (1). Priya wants all the failed slips grouped at the front so the recovery team can grab them first. She keeps one finger on the spot where the next failed slip belongs and sweeps through the tray with her other hand. Every time she spots a failed slip, she swaps it into that boundary spot and moves her boundary finger forward.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Rearranging an array of 0s and 1s so all the 0s come first means partitioning the array in place with a single-pass two-pointer method that uses constant extra space. A boundary pointer called low marks the position where the next 0 should be placed, and a scanner sweeps the entire array. Every time the scanner lands on a 0, it swaps the element to the low boundary and advances the boundary.

The correctness is straightforward: everything before the low boundary is guaranteed to be a 0 because each swap places a 0 there, and everything from low onward is whatever the scanner has not yet moved. When the scan finishes, the boundary is exactly the count of 0s, and everything from the boundary onward is a 1.

In a nightly settlement batch at the National Bank of India, each outcome is either failed (0) or cleared (1), and the recovery team needs all the failed outcomes grouped at the front for urgent retries. The batch can contain millions of outcomes on shared infrastructure with tight memory limits, so allocating a parallel array is not acceptable. The in-place partition reorganizes the batch cheaply within the settlement window.

The senior-level point is that this simple two-value partition is the foundation of the Dutch National Flag three-way partition, where three pointers segregate three groups around a pivot. Keeping the swap logic in an isolated helper makes it directly extensible to the three-pointer variant without touching the callers.

Remember one sentence: keep a low boundary for the next 0, sweep once, and swap every 0 you find up to that boundary.
